06 · Operation count of one LoRA training step (Table 2)

For a layer ||(W\in\mathbb R^{d_\text{out}\times d_\text{in}}||) and a batch ||(X\in\mathbb R^{d_\text{in}\times N}||) with upstream gradient ||(G=\partial L/\partial H\in\mathbb R^{d_\text{out}\times N}||), counting an ||(n\times m||) by ||(m\times k||) product as ||(nmk||) (elementwise operations not counted):
method forward backward
full fine-tuning ||(WX||): ||(Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||) ||(\nabla_W=GX^\top||): ||(Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||); ||(W^\top G||): ||(Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||)
LoRA, ||(B(AX)||) ||(WX||), ||(U=AX||): ||(rNd_\text{in}||), ||(BU||): ||(rNd_\text{out}||) ||(\nabla_B=GU^\top||), ||(\nabla_U=B^\top G||): ||(rNd_\text{out}||) each; ||(\nabla_A=\nabla_UX^\top||): ||(rNd_\text{in}||); ||(W^\top G+A^\top\nabla_U||)
LoRA, ||((BA)X||) ||(M=BA||): ||(rd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||); ||((W+M)X||) ||(\nabla_M=GX^\top||): ||(Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||); ||(\nabla_B,\nabla_A||): ||(rd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||) each; ||((W+M)^\top G||)
Hence, with the input gradient, LoRA ||(B(AX)||) costs ||(2Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}+3rN(d_\text{in}+d_\text{out})||) against ||(3Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||) for full fine-tuning, while ||((BA)X||) costs ||(3Nd_\text{in}d_\text{out}+3rd_\text{in}d_\text{out}||), more than full fine-tuning. Trainable parameters: ||(r(d_\text{in}+d_\text{out})||) against ||(d_\text{out}d_\text{in}+d_\text{out}||). We verify every count with PyTorch's FlopCounterMode (it reports ||(2nmk||); we divide by 2).

✔ Measured counts equal the formulas for all three methods. For this layer ||(B(AX)||) is cheaper than full fine-tuning exactly when ||(r < d_\text{in}d_\text{out}/(3(d_\text{in}+d_\text{out})) = 85.3||).
All configurations of Table 2 (every count asserted equal to its formula)

Whole-network cost of one training step of KryptoNet-40 (batch N = 64)

For LoRA on ||(W_1||) only, the backward pass must still propagate input gradients through the four frozen layers above it, so the saving is about a third — LoRA's large savings are in trainable parameters, optimiser state (two Adam moments per trainable parameter) and per-task storage.
